# teelolws/EditModeExpanded wiki: Authors: Library Usage
First, import the Library into your addon. Embed the EditModeExpanded-1.0 directory, and include EditModeExpanded-1.0.xml in your .toc or .xml
Next, EditModeExpanded needs a Saved Variable table to work with. This can be a subtable, or a table created by AceDB, or some other method. As long as you initialised the table - EME won't initialise it for you.
Create a library instance by using LibStub:
`local lib = LibStub:GetLibrary("EditModeExpanded-1.0")`
During an ADDON_LOADED event, or later - at any point after Saved Variables have been loaded, register your frame by calling this function:
`lib:RegisterFrame(frame, localizedName, db, anchorTo, anchorPoint, clamped)`
* frame - this is the Frame you want to register to be moved and resized in Edit Mode
* localizedName - this is the name of the frame you want to appear over the frame when selected during Edit Mode
* db - this is an empty table somewhere in your saved variables where the library can save size and position information about your frame between sessions
* anchorTo: frame to anchor to, default is UIParent
* anchorPoint: point to anchor, default is BOTTOMLEFT
* clamped: whether to enable "clamped to screen". default is TRUE
By default, this will add movement support to Edit Mode. To add more features, use these functions:
Call this to add a slider to the frames dialog box, allowing it to be resized using frame:SetScale
* frame: an edit mode registered frame, either one already registered by Blizz, or a custom one you have registered with lib:RegisterFrame
* minSize: minimum size, default will be 10
* maxSize: maximum size, default will be 200
* step: step size, default will be 5
`lib:RegisterResizable(frame, minSize, maxSize, step)`
Call this if you need to update the size of the frame to whatever has been set by the player from their lib:RegisterResizable setting.
`lib:UpdateFrameResize(frame)`
Call this to add a checkbox to the frames dialog box, allowing the frame to be permanently hidden outside of Edit Mode
* frame: an edit mode registered frame, either one already registered by Blizz, or a custom one you have registered with lib:RegisterFrame
* onEventHandler: optional function that is called when an event is fired for this frame, while it is shown.

...

A simple check of "has this frame been registered with EME" - maybe you want to test if another addon registered it already?
`lib:IsRegistered(frame)`
Is the Expanded frame checkbox checked for this frame, making it visible during Edit Mode?
`lib:IsFrameEnabled(frame)`

...

`lib:RegisterCustomCheckbox(frame, name, onChecked, onUnchecked, internalName)`
Use this if a frame by default doesn't have a size set yet, or the size is very small and you want the Edit Mode selection box to be bigger
`lib:SetDefaultSize(frame, x, y)`
Use this for small frames - frames that have a dimension < 40, that you don't want to be bumped up to 40 during Edit Mode
`lib:SetDontResize(frame)`
Call this if the frame needs to be moved back into position at some point after ADDON_LOADED
`lib:RepositionFrame(frame)`

...

* Prerequsities: LibDataBroker and LibDBIcon
* Must be called during PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD or later, or issues with MinimapBagButton compatibility can occur
`lib:RegisterMinimapPinnable(frame)`
Will make the frame not shown during edit mode by default
`lib:HideByDefault(frame)`

# UI and HUD Edit Mode Guide
By Zvez Updated: 2026/06/16
Show Table of Contents
Added in Dragonflight, the Heads-Up Display (HUD) Edit Mode allows players to customize their User Interface (UI) without using addons! Learn the basics of using this system to create your perfect UI!

## Getting Started
**Edit Mode** can be found by pressing your Escape key and hitting the ‘Edit Mode’ button on the game menu. The main Edit Mode menu will allow you to change your layouts, adjust your edit mode settings, and toggle certain UI elements on and off.
The main menu provides plenty of options for anyone trying to quickly create an appealing UI. However, those looking to fully customize their layout will want to check the ‘Advanced Options’ box to see toggles for important elements like the Stance Bar and Extra Action Button.
[Screenshot of HUD Edit Mode main menu](https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1219114.jpg)

## Editing Your UI Using Edit Mode
Any UI elements highlighted in blue can be adjusted using Edit Mode. Here are the basics of editing your UI:
* Selecting a UI element will bring up a sub-menu with options specific to that element.
* Element sub-menus can include quick access to other useful features like Quick Keybind Mode and the Action Bar gameplay menu!
* Selected elements can be moved by clicking and dragging them anywhere on your screen.
* Having ‘Snap to Elements’ checked in the main Edit Mode menu will cause the UI element that you’re moving to attach itself to the nearest grid line or UI element.
[Screenshot of HUD Edit Mode menu and Action Bar 1 sub-menu](https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1219112.jpg)

## Layouts
After creating your desired layout, you can save it by clicking the layout dropdown bar on the main Edit Mode menu and selecting the ‘New Layout’ option.
[Screenshot of HUD Edit Mode Layout drop down menu](https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1219113.jpg)
Here are some key features of layouts:
* Saved layouts can be named to keep them organized.
* Layouts can be made character-specific, meaning they'll only appear as an option for the associated character.
* Use the 'Share' and 'Import' options to swap layouts with others!
* Toggle between layouts using a macro.
**Layout Toggle Macro**
```
/ run x={"changeme1","changeme2"} if not p or p== then p=0 end p=p+1;  
/ run for i, l in ipairs(EditModeManagerFrame:GetLayouts()) do if l.layoutName == x[p] then EditModeManagerFrame:SelectLayout(i) end end
```
Edit 'changemeX to the name of your desired layouts.

## Cooldown Manager
Blizzard added a Cooldown Manager to Edit Mode that tracks abilities and buffs of your class. For more information on the Cooldown Manager, check out our [Cooldown Manager Guide](https://www.wowhead.com/guide/ui/cooldown-manager-setup) !
